content.title: About
content.content: Ready-to-eat cereal (NFS) consists of dry grain flakes that have been heat‑treated for instant preparation. It typically contains a blend of wheat, corn and rice, is fortified with vitamins and minerals, and may include dried fruit, nuts or sweeteners.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cereal is ready in minutes – just add milk or water and wait a short time.
There are over 100 flavor variations, from classic "honey‑nut" to exotic "mango‑coconut".
Most ready‑to‑eat cereals are fortified with B‑vitamins, iron and calcium.
Thermal processing makes the flakes crunchy and extends shelf life.
In some countries, ready‑to‑eat cereal is used as a base for energy bars.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fortified cereals provide vitamin D, iron, calcium and folic acid, supporting bone health and blood formation.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Complex carbs deliver sustained energy and help maintain satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most ready‑to‑eat cereals contain little saturated fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Whole‑grain ingredients and added fiber improve gut function and regularity.

items.title: Convenient and quick
items.content: Fast preparation helps maintain a regular eating schedule, which is important for busy lifestyles.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some varieties contain high amounts of added sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase diabetes risk.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Most cereals are wheat‑based and contain gluten, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Ingredients may include nuts, soy or dairy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Certain cereals can cause rapid spikes in blood glucose, which may be undesirable for those with insulin resistance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour milk, kefir, yogurt or a plant‑based drink over the cereal, then add fresh or dried fruit, nuts and honey. It can also serve as a base for smoothie bowls or be incorporated into baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cereal in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer to an airtight container. Shelf life is indicated on the packaging.
